'''''Withania frutescens''''' is a plant species belonging to the family [[Solanaceae]]. It is native to the western Mediterranean region, including southern [[Iberia]] (in Portugal and south and southeastern Spain), the [[Balearic Islands]], Northwest Africa (including Morocco and western Algeria) and the Canary Islands.<ref>{{cite web |title=Withania frutescens |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/11_134_04_Withania.pdf#page=2 |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref>

== Description ==
This shrub can grow up to three meters in height but typically reaches about one and a half meters.

It flowers between May and June and sheds its leaves during the summer. The [[Berry|berries]] are greenish and have a diameter of 7 to 8 mm.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Stübing |first=G. |title=Plantas silvestres de la Comunidad Valenciana |last2=Peris |first2=J. B. |date=1998 |publisher=Ediciones Jaguar |isbn=84-89960-24-0 |location=Madrid, Spain |pages=626 |language=es}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
''Withania frutescens'' was described by [[Carl Linnaeus|Linnaeus]] [[Charles Louis Constant Pauquy|Pauquy]] and published in ''De la Belladone . . .'' ''Paris 14'', in 1825.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Withania frutescens |url=https://www.tropicos.org/Name/29600086 |access-date= |website=Trópicos}}</ref>
